- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecasts rise sharply, cap the upward slope to avoid overshoot after spikes.
- If official supply net is negative and sentiment is mixed or bearish, reduce forecast mean by 2–5% to account for policy-induced downward pressure.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior period), model should slow trend decay to avoid overcorrection; add 1–2 days of lagged momentum decay.
- When bullish events outnumber bearish (net bullish > 0), forecast should be slightly higher than historical mean, but not exceed 1.5σ above to avoid overconfidence.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative swings (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative sentiment), model should adjust downward by 0.5–1.0% per negative sentiment event.
- For high-event periods (≥15 events/30d), reduce forecast slope by 10–20% to account for event noise and mean reversion toward prior 10-day average.
- When policy_count > 0, reduce forecast by 1–3% to reflect regulatory uncertainty or supply-side constraints.
